title: Forty-eight ways (Avot 6:6)
hookLine: Torah is acquired by a listening ear, ordered speech, an understanding heart, and forty-five more
tomorrow: you repeat a friend's great line. whose line is it now?

cards: A job posting lists forty-eight requirements, and most of us would close the tab. Avot 6:6 has a list like that, and it opens with a comparison. Kingship is acquired with thirty qualities.
Priesthood with twenty-four. Torah with forty-eight. It reads almost like a scoreboard, and the book wins by a lot.
That's the odd detail. Why would a book of teaching take more to get than a throne?

teach.b: Start with how a king and a priest got the job in the Bible. David's line held the crown. Aaron's sons held the priesthood.
You were born into them, or you weren't.
Now read the forty-eight. The list opens: with study, with a listening ear, with ordered speech, with an understanding heart.
Further down: with humility, with joy, with serving the sages, with the give-and-take of friends and students, loving rebuke, being happy with your portion. None of them comes with a family name.
Each one is something a person does, or slowly becomes. That's the puzzle solved. A crown is handed down.
Torah, in this list, can only be acquired, so the list is long, and the door is open.
Now notice what sits near the very top, second only to study: a listening ear. In Hebrew, shmi'at ha-ozen, the hearing of the ear.
Before ordered speech, before an understanding heart, the list asks you to hear.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in Avot, a throne takes thirty qualities and Torah takes forty-eight, and not one of the forty-eight needs the right parents.
The student in the back row who never gets called on can start with number two.

how: In a yeshiva or a study group, much of learning happens out loud in pairs, so listening to a partner's reading is part of the work; many people also study Avot's sixth chapter, with its forty-eight ways, on Shabbat afternoons.

o: the forty-eight laws a king must keep while on the throne
Avot's list of the qualities by which Torah is acquired
the paths a pilgrim once walked around the Temple

games.q: Avot 6:6, piece by piece — tap the pairs.

s: in Avot, Torah belongs to those born into the right family
the opposite: a crown and a priesthood come by birth, and every one of the forty-eight ways is something a person does.
Avot says kingship takes thirty qualities and priesthood twenty-four
and Torah takes forty-eight, more than either.
the list starts with being naturally clever
it starts with study, then a listening ear, then ordered speech and an understanding heart.

games.q: a group meeting where everyone talks over each other and nothing gets decided. you have a strong idea. which of the forty-eight comes first?
o: a listening ear: hear what's been said before adding yours.
ordered speech: say your idea clearly enough to win the room.
happy with your portion: let the others decide and stay out of it.
games.why: all three are on the list, but the listening ear comes before ordered speech. hearing first is the step most of us skip.

practice: Close your eyes if you like, and listen. Find the farthest sound you can hear, then the nearest, then the quietest one in between. Don't name them or judge them; just receive each one, the way the list asks an ear to.
If someone nearby is talking, let their voice be one of the sounds, and hear the words without answering them.

wordCard.voice: Forty-eight ways. Avot's list of how Torah is acquired: more than a crown's thirty, and every one open to anyone.

orig.note: Hebrew: the hearing of the ear, a listening ear, second of Avot's forty-eight ways.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: a listening ear, second on the list and open to anyone. One day of Avot left.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 6:6 (Torah is greater than priesthood and kingship: thirty, twenty-four, forty-eight; the list of the forty-eight)
Numbers 18:1–7; 2 Samuel 7:12–16 (priesthood to Aaron's sons; the kingdom to David's line)
